result.title: Do 3D Point Representations Encode Architectural Functions? Probing Supervised and Pretrained Models on Urban Facades
result.comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop: Physical World AI: Geometry, Characteristics, and Multimodal Sensing
result.summary: Semantic labels say what a building element is, not what it does: two identical-looking windows on one facade may be operable or fixed, a column may carry load or only decorate. We ask whether 3D point representations encode such architectural function. On 22 mobile-LiDAR buildings with 15 functional attributes per element, we hold out entire buildings and compare hand-crafted descriptors, networks trained from scratch and frozen self-supervised point transformers. Descriptors and frozen features are read by the same linear layer. No network trained from scratch, from PointNet to a 108M-parameter PTv3, clearly exceeds the descriptors (0.610 mAP on functionally ambiguous elements), whereas frozen Utonia reaches 0.732. Random-weight controls of the same architectures (0.649 and 0.652) attribute the gain to pretraining (Utonia: +0.080, 95% building interval [+0.035, +0.124]). Pretrained features improve at every tested number of labelled buildings while descriptors and random features plateau, and, in the configurations we tested, fine-tuning erodes the benefit: at today's data scale, function is better read from pretrained representations than learned from scratch.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在22栋移动LiDAR采集的城市立面上，用统一的线性读出比较手工描述子、从头训练的3D网络与冻结的自监督点云Transformer能否解码15种建筑功能属性，并以随机权重对照将增益归因于预训练。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「统一线性探针＋随机权重基线」的表征归因做法，可能可供核查LVR中视觉细节与任务必要信息是否确实保留在内部状态、以及表现提升究竟来自预训练表征还是训练过程；但对象为3D点云静态属性而非推理状态生成。
